name: Watch GitHub incident recovery
prompt: Classify changes from the normalized githubstatus.com monitor snapshot. The monitor provides a unified diff and the complete new JSON snapshot. Use only that data; do not call tools or infer beyond GitHub's official status. On the first baseline run, when there is no previous output, respond exactly [SILENT]. Also respond exactly [SILENT] for source_health-only changes, source errors, wording-only changes, or changes with no meaningful usability impact. Notify Bryan when GitHub meaningfully improves or worsens. Improvement includes: the overall indicator improves; an incident advances from investigating to identified, monitoring, or resolved/disappears; an affected component improves from major_outage to partial_outage, degraded_performance, or operational/disappears; or an official latest_update explicitly reports recovery or restored service. Worsening includes: the overall indicator degrades; a new incident appears; an incident regresses to investigating or increases in impact; an affected component degrades from operational/disappeared to degraded_performance, partial_outage, or major_outage; or an official latest_update explicitly reports a regression, renewed disruption, or additional affected service. For a meaningful change, begin the final response exactly `@bryan:snowboardtechie.com`, lead with what improved or worsened, name the exact services and statuses that changed, briefly state what remains affected, and end with the raw link https://www.githubstatus.com/. Say fully resolved only when the new snapshot has overall indicator `none`, no incidents, and no affected_components. Keep the message concise.
